messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PG-DB-CONN-EXHAUSTION (sev=high). Service: postgres-primary.redwood-prod. Trigger: connection_count > 480 for 2m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PAGE-12345

pagerduty-bot: Paging on-call: alexa (oncall) at +1 555-0100 (escalation rule: 1st minute then team).

alexa (oncall): ack. looking. grabbing metrics.

samir: seeing a spike in total_connections on the primary: `connections=512/512 max=512`. apps hitting the DB hard. any recent deploy?

mei: no deploys in last 2 hours. background job queue (worker-sync) had a backlog bump ~15m ago though.

luis (sre): can you `kubectl get pods -n infra pgbouncer-*` ? wondering if pooling dropped.

alexa (oncall): running:```
kubectl get pods -n infra | grep pgbouncer
pgbouncer-0   1/1 Running   0     3d
pgbouncer-1   1/1 Running   0     3d
```

alexa (oncall): metrics: `pg.connections_total 512`, `pg.waiting_clients 120`, `pg.deadlocks 0`. DB logs show: `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`.

samir: that means app pool trying to open too many clients. which services are most active?

alexa (oncall): query from grafana: top connecters -> gen-api (220 conns), ingest-workers (150), embeddings-service (80), rest is misc.

rachel (cs): are customers impacted? getting a support ticket about 503s for embedding calls.

alexa (oncall): yes, some customer-facing endpoints are 502/503ing when DB returns "connection refused". marking customer-impacting. pinging CS. @rachel can you triage top affected customers and put in status page if needed?

rachel (cs): yes, putting a short note on status: "Intermittent errors for some inference/embedding requests. Investigating." Will DM impacted customers after we have ETA.

luis (sre): quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle app side connection creation via feature flag (limit pool size) 2) increase pgbouncer max_client_conn temporarily and reload 3) move read-heavy traffic to replica if possible 4) postpone background jobs. any objections?

mei: I can flip the worker-sync pause flag. will do now.

alexa (oncall): doing app-side throttle: patching k8s config for gen-api and embeddings to set DB_POOL_MAX=20 (was 50). applying with rolling restart (keep concurrency low).

alexa (oncall): patch applied to gen-api and embeddings; starting rolling restart. monitoring connections.

opsbot: configmap updated for gen-api: DB_POOL_MAX=20. Rollout started.

luis (sre): increasing pgbouncer max_client_conn from 10000 to 15000 on both pods and reloading.```
kubectl exec -n infra pgbouncer-0 -- pgbouncer -R && kubectl exec -n infra pgbouncer-1 -- pgbouncer -R
```

alexa (oncall): after app throttles and pgbouncer reload: connections dropped to ~260, waiting_clients down to 10. errors reduced. embedding errors still trickling.

samir: runbook step: if connections spike again, scale pgbouncer horizontally (add a 3rd replica) and add traffic-split to LB. Also consider enabling client-side queueing.

alexa (oncall): scaling pgbouncer to 3 replicas now.```
kubectl scale deploy pgbouncer --replicas=3 -n infra
```

alexa (oncall): scaled. new pod joining, connections redistributed. overall connections ~180 now. 5m since mitigation started.

rachel (cs): CS update posted to status. customers responding; asking for ETA. I'll share "investigating, mitigation underway, no ETA yet".

luis (sre): follow-up TODOs: add circuit-breaker on gen-api for DB errors; add retry/backoff for embeddings; implement connection pool limits as default.

alexa (oncall): summary so far: cause = burst of background jobs + mis-sized app pools. mitigation = paused jobs, app-side pool throttles, pgbouncer reload + scale. user impact = intermittent 502/503 for embedding endpoints; CS notified.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by alexa (oncall) at 1774218912.

opsbot: created incident ticket: INC-2026-0456, assigned to eng-sre.

mei: continuing to watch. will reopen background jobs slowly once connections stable.

alexa (oncall): 25m in, metrics stable. connections at 140, waiting_clients 2. embedding errors down to <1% of normal.

samir: can we run a quick diag query to ensure no lingering idle sessions?```
SELECT usename, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle in transaction' GROUP BY usename;
```

alexa (oncall): ran => no abnormal long-running active sessions. most idle.

rachel (cs): customers updated: some thanked for fast response. one large customer asked for postmortem.

luis (sre): I'll take postmortem lead. plan: root cause = unbounded worker-sync spawn + pooled clients per worker not limited. action items: default DB_POOL_MAX=25 across services, add alert for pg.waiting_clients > 50, autoscale pgbouncer based on queued clients, add playbook step to pause workers automated on spike. assign owners.

alexa (oncall): handing off on-call to samir for follow-up. I'm heading to a meeting. Handoff: systems stable, mitigation in place, INC-2026-0456 created, postmortem owner luis.

samir: ack. monitoring. will keep CS looped in.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved -> PG-DB-CONN-EXHAUSTION at 1774219273. Resolved reason: manual mitigations and scaling reduced connection pressure.

alexa (oncall): marking thread resolved. leaving notes in incident ticket. good job team :thumbsup:
